See also: nōdo

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
nodo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin nōdus.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈnodo/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Rhymes: -odo
  • Syllabification: no‧do

Noun

[edit]

nodo (accusative singular nodon, plural nodoj, accusative plural nodojn)

  1. knot (looping of a piece of string or any other long, flexible material)
  2. knot (whorl in wood)
  3. (astronomy, mathematics) node

Further reading

[edit]
  • “nodo”, in Plena Ilustrita Vortaro de Esperanto [Complete Illustrated Dictionary of Esperanto], 2020, →ISBN
  • “nodo”, in Reta Vortaro [Online Dictionary] (in Esperanto), 1997-2026

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin nōdus, English node, French nœud, Italian nodo, Spanish nudo.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈnodo/

Noun

[edit]

nodo (plural nodi)

  1. knot

Italian

[edit]
Italian Wikipedia has an article on:
nodo
Wikipedia it

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin nōdus, from Proto-Indo-European *gned-, *gnod- (“to bind”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈnɔ.do/
  • Rhymes: -ɔdo
  • Hyphenation: nò‧do
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

nodo m (plural nodi)

  1. knot, gnarl
  2. bond, tie
  3. node, vertex
  4. crux
  5. road junction
  6. (unit of measure) knot
  7. lump
  8. bend

Derived terms

[edit]
  • annodare
  • linfonodo
  • nodino (e.g. a knot of mozzarella or a chop of beef)
  • nodo linfatico
  • nodoso
  • snodare

Anagrams

[edit]
  • dono, donò, ondo, ondò

Japanese

[edit]

Romanization

[edit]

nodo

  1. Rōmaji transcription of のど

Latin

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

From nōdus (“knot”) +‎ -ō.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Classical Latin) IPA(key): [ˈnoː.doː]
  • (modern Italianate Ecclesiastical) IPA(key): [ˈnɔː.do]

Noun

[edit]

nōdō m

  1. dative/ablative singular of nōdus

Verb

[edit]

nōdō (present infinitive nōdāre, perfect active nōdāvī, supine nōdātum); first conjugation

  1. to knot, make knotted, tie in a knot

Portuguese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin nōdus. Doublet of nó.

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈnɔ.du/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈnɔ.du/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈnɔ.do/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /ˈnɔ.du/ [ˈnɔ.ðu]

  • Hyphenation: no‧do

Noun

[edit]

nodo m (plural nodos)

  1. (graph theory) node (vertex of a graph)
    Synonym: nó
  2. (medicine) node (growth formed around bones)
  3. (astronomy) node (point where the orbit of a planet intersects the ecliptic)
  4. (physics) node (point in a standing wave with the lowest or null amplitude)
    Synonym: nó

Further reading

[edit]
  • “nodo”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “nodo”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “nodo”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
  • “nodo”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

  • IPA(key): /ˈnodo/ [ˈno.ð̞o]
  • Rhymes: -odo
  • Syllabification: no‧do

Noun

[edit]

nodo m (plural nodos)

  1. node
